name: add_tests_express_multi
description: Asks the model to write in-process tests for an order-classification Express API; mutation-checked
prompts: This Express app (src/app.js mounts src/routes/orders.js, backed by the classify() rule in src/services/orders.js - already correct, do not modify anything under src/) exposes POST /orders. Rules: a priority order is tier 'express' (fee 20) regardless of size; otherwise items>=10 is 'bulk' (fee 5); otherwise 'standard' (fee 10). The JSON response is { items, tier, fee }. Write tests in a file named exactly test_orders.js: require('./src/app'), start it on an EPHEMERAL port with app.listen(0) (do not hardcode a port), and use Node's built-in http and assert modules (no supertest - it is not installed) to check at least: a small non-priority order is standard/10; items==10 is bulk/5 (the boundary); a priority order is express/20; and a priority order with items>=10 is still express (priority wins). Close the server after each request. Print PASS and exit 0 when all assertions hold; let a failure exit non-zero.

test_setup_files.mutation_check.py:
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

IMPL = Path("src/services/orders.js")
TEST_CMD = "node test_orders.js"
MUTANTS = [[["  else if (items >= 10) tier = 'bulk';", "  else if (items >= 100) tier = 'bulk';"]], [["  const fee = { express: 20, bulk: 5, standard: 10 }[tier];", "  const fee = { express: 20, bulk: 10, standard: 10 }[tier];"]]]

def run_tests():
    return subprocess.run(TEST_CMD, shell=True).returncode

src = IMPL.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
for group in MUTANTS:
    for old, _new in group:
        assert src.count(old) == 1, (
            f"protected implementation file {IMPL} was modified - the task said not to change it "
            f"(anchor not found exactly once: {old!r})")

rc = run_tests()
assert rc == 0, f"model tests FAILED against the correct implementation (exit {rc})"

try:
    for i, group in enumerate(MUTANTS, 1):
        mutated = src
        for old, new in group:
            mutated = mutated.replace(old, new)
        IMPL.write_text(mutated, encoding="utf-8")
        rc = run_tests()
        assert rc != 0, (
            f"mutation {i} SURVIVED: the tests still pass against a deliberately broken "
            f"implementation, so they do not actually verify the required behavior")
finally:
    IMPL.write_text(src, encoding="utf-8")

print("PASS (tests pass on correct impl and kill all {n} mutants)".format(n=len(MUTANTS)))
